description: Unlike the worded `is a <type-word>` (whose type word is grammar-checked at parse time), the prefix `is_a?` evaluates its second argument dynamically: a non-word type argument raises `ol-type` naming the expected concept "word" (`spec/commands.md:708`, `spec/error-model.md` `ol-type`). The check finds nothing here, so Phase 2 begins and execution halts at the failing statement, keeping the `instruction` event asserted below — the fault is genuinely runtime, not check-caught. Issue #99. Issue #1156 corrected two things this description used to carry: a denial that this statement executed at all, which contradicted the event asserted below (pasted from `core-language/execution/is-a-unknown-type`, the check-caught worded-form fixture, where both of its clauses are measured true), and a citation of `spec/commands.md:691-705` — a range holding the `is_a?` entry's heading and example but NOT the "Possible errors" row that names `ol-type`, which is `:708`.
